verdict.rationale: YYLO Skills is a skill pack installed into coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Pi. It lets those agents act on user requests, such as using Ledger Records, planning work or inspecting a project before a requested change, so a user can drive YYLO tooling through an agent conversation. However, no evidence explicitly documents natural-language command handling; the documented interfaces are CLI flags and single-letter shortcuts. missing for 10: explicit documentation of natural-language invocation, example prompts mapped to actions, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Seven independently versioned Skills help agents use Ledger Records, understand projects, plan work, and deliver one bounded task.
Inspect the current product architecture, dependencies, and validation loops before planning or implementing a requested change.
Install all skills for Claude Code, Codex, and Pi without prompts
